leads.title: MIBRAG: EU strategic-reserve provision applied to German network-reserve return
leads.process: Federal proposal for market return of network-reserve power stations; exact legislative vehicle/draft remains a scope gate

claim_quote.translation_en: Translation: not covered by the Electricity Market Regulation.

locator.section: Fazit, final sentence on reserve-plant market return to reduce price peaks

leads.context: The one-page statement expressly concerns Steinkohle plants from the Netzreserve, quotes Regulation 2019/943 Article 22(2)(a),(d),(e) on a capacity mechanism designed as a strategic reserve, and distinguishes the 2022/2023 gas-security emergency. It objects to the proposal as legally unsupported and competitively harmful.
leads.why_worth_checking: The legal conclusion centrally supports outright rejection and depends on whether German network-reserve installations and the proposed return mechanism fall within the quoted strategic-capacity-reserve category. A category mismatch would be distinct from a disagreement about competitive effects.
leads.plausible_benign_explanation: The actual proposed mechanism may legally constitute a strategic capacity reserve, or additional provisions/state-aid conditions may impose the same restriction. Network-reserve and capacity-reserve labels alone cannot resolve the EU-law classification. The submission may be a general policy paper outside an identifiable legislative consultation.

deprioritised_after_primary_check.title: GDA: foreign technical-standard description supporting load-dependent PUE compliance
deprioritised_after_primary_check.process: EnEfG/EED implementation, government bill BT 21/8027; author October 5, 2026 post-hearing elaboration

claim_quote.translation_en: Translation: at 25, 50, 75 and 100 percent of the IT design load.

locator.section: I, Internationale Einordnung; sentence about ASHRAE Standard 90.4.

deprioritised_after_primary_check.context: The full response acknowledges that PUE is an energy ratio and that lower PUE need not reduce absolute consumption. It proposes a verified design/load curve, operating checks and remediation, keeps the fixed-limit route, and alternatively asks for 1.3 instead of 1.2. Its claim that ASHRAE 90.4 assesses both mechanical and electrical infrastructure at four stated IT load points is a specific source description, not merely an opinion about PUE.
deprioritised_after_primary_check.why_worth_checking: The asserted international precedent directly supports a new compliance route. Check the particular ASHRAE edition, whether electrical and mechanical metrics have identical load points and whether a component-efficiency standard is comparable to the proposed PUE curve. This is a technical source-scope check, not a claim that load-dependent regulation is unwise.
deprioritised_after_primary_check.plausible_benign_explanation: The four load points may be correct for the relevant edition or rating paths; compressed wording may reasonably summarise different component tests. Singapore Green Mark may independently support the proposal even if ASHRAE differs.

next_primary_evidence.source: Original ASHRAE Standard 90.4 edition operative at October 2026 and official addenda
next_primary_evidence.task: Compare the mechanical/electrical compliance and partial-load tables. Identify any paid-access limitation rather than infer an error.

next_primary_evidence.task: Independently test the second expressly cited international precedent.

claim_quote.original: Die Stromgestehungskosten wachsen um bis zu 30 Prozent an
claim_quote.translation_en: Translation: The levelised costs of electricity rise by up to 30 percent.

locator.paragraph: Second main paragraph, explicitly introducing the Prognos study results.
Same paragraph, proposed new starting bid cap effective January 1, 2027; operative amendment follows.

deprioritised_after_primary_check.context: The submission expressly treats regulatory measures as planned and reports cumulative effects from several studies. It links the selected Prognos figures to a demand to raise the 2027 PV auction cap from 5.9 to at least 7 ct/kWh. The page also assigns new AgNes capacity charges to January 1, 2027, a separately checkable timetable premise. No error has been established.
deprioritised_after_primary_check.why_worth_checking: A named, publicly linked model supports a concrete statutory monetary request. Check whether the stated 30 percent increase and 1.3–1.5 ct/kWh excess describe LCOE, required bids, the same PV cohort and a cumulative scenario actually modelled together. Distinguish source-description errors from disputed assumptions.
deprioritised_after_primary_check.plausible_benign_explanation: The source may match exactly; a high-cost cumulative scenario or bid/LCOE distinction could explain apparently different headline numbers. Planned regulatory dates may be scenario assumptions rather than a representation of adopted law.

next_primary_evidence.task: Read the full September 2026 Prognos report, scenario definitions, figure units and PV tables; compare exact stated figures.
Check the exact addressed government bill, section 37b and commencement provisions.

next_primary_evidence.task: Verify whether January 1, 2027 is adopted, proposed or merely assumed; no result presumed.
